title: `clr_mix()` fixes
description:
Hi @EmilHvitfeldt, when I recently found myself browsing through your `clr_mix()` function, I noticed a few things that I would like to report back.

- maybe it's worth adding
  ```
  if (!all(ratio >= 0 & ratio <= 1)) {
    stop("`ratio` must be between 0 and 1.")
  }
  ```
- you may want to document: 
  ```
  @return A colors object of the same length as `col`.
  ```
- you would be a little more efficient by putting `stop()`s at the beginning
- if you don't mind, I would be happy if the rainbow palette were replaced by one that "laymen" are less likely to do harm with

In the tests I find a few irritating things some of which may be typos and copy-and-paste mistakes:
- in "`clr_mix()` *preserves* length" you could be more specific by e.g. "returns color object of correct length and hex codes" and adjust tests accordingly
- I suggest being more specific in `expect_error()` `col` type tests by e.g. adding the expected message and separating type from invalid color
- "`clr_mix()` if the length  of `mix_in` isn't 1": is not what the tests do. you may put "if `ratio` isn't length 1" and "if `mix_in` isn't length 1" (you do so) in "returns color object of correct length and hex codes" and dedicated "error..." tests
- "`clr_mix()` setting severity outside range gives error" - remove as there is no `severity` and add (as just mentioned above) test for appropriate error if `ratio` isn't between 0 and 1
- when expecting user input with `ratio = 0` and `ratio = 1` replace words severity and shift by ratio

And in the README: if you like you can use the native pipe, and thus remove the {magrittr} dependency.

description:

title: Easy way to manipulate individual hcl axes?
Include text contrast function?
Use hcl instead of hsl?
description:
I noticed that `rotate()` uses hsl rather than hcl, but my recollection is that hcl is more perceptually uniform, so I think it would be better to use hcl. 

I was also surprised see that "HSL" is the default in `clr_lighten()` — I re-read the colorspace paper to check that I wasn't missing something, but I see:

> HLS() (Hue-Lightness-Saturation) is another transformation of (s)RGB that tries to capture the perceptual axes. It does a somewhat better job but the dimensions are still strongly confounded. See Wikipedia (2019f) for more details.

title: Make `clr_` functions work within mutate?
description:
hi friend! 👋 thanks for this package, it's very very useful!

right now it doesn't look like `clr_lighten()` and `clr_darken()` (maybe all of them? I'm only looking at the lighten/darken functions though) work well within a mutate, seemingly due to mismatch in length of the colour/shift arguments. curious if this is something you'd be open to supporting, or if I'm missing some way to do it! ty!

``` r
library(prismatic)
library(dplyr)

x <- c("#fbbcb8", "#bfdff6")
clr_darken(x)
#> <colors>
#> #CE170CFF #1B7BC0FF

# sad in mutate() though
colours <- tibble(color = x) %>%
  mutate(darker = clr_darken(color))
#> Error: Problem with `mutate()` input `darker`.
#> x The length of `col` must be positive.
#> ℹ Input `darker` is `clr_darken(color)`.

# rowwise() doesn't help much?
colours <- tibble(color = x) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(darker = clr_darken(color))
#> Error: Problem with `mutate()` input `darker`.
#> x The length of `col` must be positive.
#> ℹ Input `darker` is `clr_darken(color)`.
#> ℹ The error occured in row 2.
```
